text.p: Financier Carl Icahn Friday called Marvel Entertainment Group Inc's Chapter 11 bankruptcy a ploy by Marvel investor Ron Perelman to secure a "windfall profit" for himself at the expense of others.
Icahn, through his High River Ltd Parnership, holds an undisclosed amount of Marvel bonds.
Perelman's spokesman could not be reached for comment.
Marvel Entertainment, which publishes comic books including Spider Man and the X-Men, and its three holding companies Friday filed for reorganization under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code.

The bankruptcy filing would allow Marvel to carry out a $525 million recapitalization plan. The proposal would dilute the public stockholders' ownership in Marvel, but would protect investor Ron Perelman's stake in the struggling company.

"It is patently clear that Ron Perelman has adopted this course to realize a windfall profit for himself at the expense of those to whom he owes a fiduciary responsibility," Icahn said in a statement.

"We find it unconscionable that the Andrews Group Inc, which controls Marvel, should attempt to use the bankruptcy process to wipe out its shareholders and its public bondholders from whom it borrowed over $800 million in good faith only a few years ago," Icahn said.
"We find it especially reprehensible that Marvel has adopted this course and completely ignored a far more equitable alternative that had been presented and remains available," Icahn said.
Andrews declined comment on Icahn's statements.
Icahn was not available to elaborate on the statement.
Holders of Marvel holding company bonds were asked more than a month ago to support Marvel's reorganization plan by waiving certain restrictions contained in the bonds.

Bondholders balked at financier Perelman's proposal to buy newly issued shares of Marvel at a steep discount to the market. The move would massively dilute the value of Marvel's current stock, which backs the company's bonds.
